_doc: Honest contract-implementation debt baseline. The gate previously had no baseline at all: check-contract-implementation.sh defaulted its threshold to 0 (so it ALWAYS failed) while run-api-contract-checks.sh tried to set 999999 but never exported it (so the guard never saw it) and then swallowed the failure with `|| gate_warn`. The result was a gate that was permanently red AND permanently non-blocking — ignored either way. This ledger records the measured truth so the gate blocks REGRESSIONS above it. INTENT: ratchet every number DOWN. Never raise a baseline to absorb new debt.
ratchetLog: 2026-08-08 established at 1399 (implemented 4903 of 4936; missing 94; orphanHandlers 1305; unownedContract 23). These are NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly created. Two compensating defects had been hiding them. (1) extractClassBase never resolved class-level @RequestMapping prefixes, so handler routes were bare fragments; findOrphanHandlers skips any route not starting with /internal|/v1|/api, and a fragment like '/{equipment_id}' fails that test, so almost no handler could ever be reported orphaned. (2) routeMatchesOperation accepted a raw-string SUFFIX match in either direction guarded only by `length > 1`, so those same fragments suffix-matched unrelated operations and reported contracts as implemented on a coincidence. Fixing the extractor alone took violations 76 -> 1413; retuning the matcher on top gives 1399.

2026-08-08 matcher retune detail: matching is now exact and segment-aligned against the three forms contracts in this repo actually use — the full route path; the CONTROLLER-RELATIVE path (many contracts declare '/{modelId}' or '/' and leave the base to `servers:`); and the same path under a different transport prefix (/external/v1/x for a route served at /internal/v1/x). Raw substring suffixes never match again. Exact-only matching was measured first and REJECTED: it reported implemented 2015 / missing 2982, because it cannot see the relative-path convention — that number was an artifact of the matcher, not a finding. Validated by controls in both directions: asset-registry's 33 /equipment orphan handlers are still caught (the contract declares 11 paths, none for /equipment), and its 14 real operations still match the correct handler files.

2026-08-08 KNOWN CONTAMINATION, not yet paid down: experience-bff.openapi.yaml contains unprefixed fragment paths ('/landela/templates', '/landela/documents/publish') that look generated by the handler-sync scripts WHILE the extractor was broken. Those contract entries are wrong at the source and should be regenerated, not matched around. Counting them here rather than tolerating them in the matcher is deliberate.
knownBlindSpots: orphanHandlers is gated by contractPathPrefixes: a handler whose path shares no leading /a/b prefix with any contract operation is skipped entirely, so a controller in a wholly undocumented namespace is invisible rather than orphaned.
experience-bff is in ORPHAN_CHECK_SKIP_MODULES, so BFF handlers are never checked for orphan status at all — only its contract operations are checked for implementation.

The controller-relative fallback is module-scoped, not controller-scoped. Within one module, a contract op declared as '/{id}' can match a root-level handler in a different controller of that same module. It answers 'an implementation exists', not 'this exact handler implements it'.

A contract operation and a route matching by transport-prefix swap (/external/v1 vs /internal/v1) are treated as the same endpoint. If a service genuinely exposes only the internal variant, the external contract operation still reads as implemented.
